direction_note: Cycle 5: scrapped fx_volume_climax_reversal (tick volume is quoted size, not a capitulation signal; shock days on EURUSD continue at the one-day horizon, fade -0.10 R t -2.5 on 245 trades; do not reuse volume or register the snooped follow) and gold_autumn_physical_demand (Baur's September/November months lost -0.04 R t -1.9 in design while the all-other-months control was flat; gold month seasonals are dead). Registered one hypothesis chosen for power: carry_cross_weekend_premium, long AUDJPY/NZDJPY/AUDUSD/NZDUSD from Friday afternoon to Monday morning with a Monday-to-Tuesday overnight control, 412 design trades per arm. Critic: revise (triple rollover is Wednesday so the premium must be price-only; weekend-edge spreads 3-4 pips round trip; exit at the open of the first bar at or after exit time; 2020 rule additive; paired fri-minus-mon t and 3-of-4 market rule; max_bars 24). Amended before any run; a second amendment after the build accepted the Builder's correct finding that skipping an entry because its future exit bar is missing is a look-ahead. Code review approved. Result: killed at stage A on AUDJPY. All 16 arms negative in design; the eight Friday weekend arms have design t -1.2 to -2.5 and the Monday overnight controls -0.5 to -4.3; the check period is flat (-0.02 to +0.006 R). Lesson for the scrap index: there is no weekend risk premium in carry crosses net of costs in 2010-2017, and no weekday overnight premium either; holding yen crosses or AUD/NZD across the Friday-to-Monday gap costs the spread and earns nothing. This was the first adequately powered test in three cycles and it is an honest negative. Programme assessment for the user: cycles 3-5 tested six mechanisms (two rejected pre-compute, four killed at stage A) across cross-asset, central-bank flow, tick volume, calendar-month, and weekend-hold dimensions; with the atlas, the alpha hunt and the pattern searches before them, the price-and-clock hypothesis space reachable with this data store is close to exhausted. Further cycles are unlikely to find a new FX edge without external inputs (retail positioning, options risk reversals, FX swap basis, a scheduled-event calendar), and the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, a simulation task (gj-strat prop_sim, prop_risk_rules), not a hypothesis. Recommend the user decide whether to pause the loop, add external data, or redirect the next cycles to basket sizing.

judgments.lesson: Tick volume is not a capitulation signal on FX. Dukascopy volume is summed quoted size: its 20-day ratio rarely exceeds 1.7 even on crisis days, so climax arms hold 10-50 design trades and cannot be read. The no-filter control (v = 0) measured the plain one-day shock reversal on EURUSD for the first time in this programme: fading a one-day move >= 1 x ATR20 LOSES -0.10 R (t -2.5, 245 design trades) and -0.18 R at 1.25 x ATR20, so shock days on majors continue rather than reverse at the one-day horizon, extending cross_zfade's lesson from crosses to majors; the volume filter only softened that loss (v = 1.3: -0.08 to -0.21 R on 43-46 trades). Do not reuse tick volume as a signal input, and do not register the 'follow the shock' mirror: its sign was read off this run's control arm, and the check period of that arm was near zero (-0.04 R fade), so the mirror would be a snooped flip with no out-of-sample support.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on EURUSD; the pooled stage B never ran, so the clustered multi-market question is unanswered but not worth another trial at these sample sizes. Process note recorded in the cycle 4 log: the Builder went back twice on one blocker.

judgments.lesson: Gold calendar-month seasonals are dead for this programme. Baur's autumn effect (long gold in September and November) tested out of sample with an all-other-months control: the published months LOST in design (-0.040 R per 23-hour trade, t -1.9, 275 trades; September-November -0.036 R, t -2.2, 416 trades) while the rest-of-year control was flat (0.000 R, 1228 trades), so the effect reversed sign after 2010 rather than fading. Do not retry with other month windows, Chinese New Year windows, Diwali-date windows, or a short-the-weak-season mirror.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on XAUUSD. The control design worked as intended: the drift question (gold's trend vs seasonal demand) was answered without ambiguity because the control was flat and the window negative.

hypotheses.title: Weekend risk premium in carry crosses: long AUDJPY (NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD) from the Friday New York afternoon to the Monday Tokyo or London open, with a weekday-overnight control
hypotheses.rationale: Leveraged carry positions (Japanese retail margin books, CTAs, macro funds) cannot be adjusted for about 48 hours over the weekend, and weekend gap risk in the yen crosses is the largest in FX (the Monday-gap column of the market facts shows AUDJPY 1.2, NZDJPY 2.0, GBPJPY 3.9 pips median, with the tails far larger). Risk managers therefore cut high-yield exposure into the Friday New York afternoon and re-establish it on Monday in Tokyo and London; dealers widen and run flat inventory over the weekend and buy back Monday. The holder who carries the risk over the weekend is paid twice: the weekend swap (three days of positive carry on a long AUDJPY or NZDJPY) and the price premium from Friday selling and Monday buying. This is the FX analogue of the weekend and overnight risk premia documented in equities (Lou, Polk and Skouras 2019) and of the 'weekend effect' literature in currencies (Yamori and Kurihara 2004), which the flow atlas could not see: its windows were intraday (30 minutes to 8 hours) on single weekdays, so a Friday-to-Monday hold was never measured, and no prior report in the index holds a position over a weekend by design (the gap tests measured Monday gap fills, not the weekend return). Costs are low: one spread plus slippage (AUDJPY 0.9 + 0.4 pips) against a 1.5-3 x ATR20 stop of 120-240 pips, about 0.01 R. Sample: every weekend, so about 410 design trades per market, which is why this family was chosen after cycles 3 and 4 died at the underpowered single-market gate. A weekday-overnight control is built into the grid: the same hold from Monday 20:00 UTC to Tuesday morning measures the overnight carry drift without the weekend, so the weekend premium must beat it. EURJPY is included as a low-carry comparison: if EURJPY shows the same premium the effect is a JPY-risk premium rather than carry, which is still tradeable but changes the interpretation.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: H1, labelled by open time; a bar's close time is ts + 1h. Bars are sparse; locate by timestamp.

ENTRY DAY: entry_day is a string parameter: "fri" (the hypothesis) or "mon" (the weekday-overnight control). For each UTC date D whose weekday equals entry_day, let S be the last H1 bar whose close time is at or before entry_utc on D and after entry_utc minus 2 hours (so a stale bar cannot stand in for the entry time); if none exists, no trade on D.

ENTRY: entry_long[S] = True, entry_type 0 (market at the next bar's open), valid_bars 1. One trade per entry date. Longs only (long the high-yield currency: AUDJPY, NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, EURJPY are all quoted so that a long is long the first currency, which is the higher-yielding side in 2010-2023 for AUD and NZD; EURJPY is the low-carry comparison).

STOP: sl_dist[S] = sl_atr * ATR20_prev, ATR20_prev = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), 20) mapped to S; no trade if NaN or <= 0. tp_dist = NaN. A gap through the stop at the Sunday/Monday open exits at that open (executor rule).

EXIT: let D_exit be the next UTC date after D that is a Monday when entry_day = "fri", or the next UTC date (Tuesday) when entry_day = "mon". Let X be the first H1 bar whose close time is at or after exit_utc on D_exit; set exit_long[X - 1] = True if X - 1 > S (so the position closes at the open of bar X, i.e. at exit_utc or the first bar after it). If no such bar exists within D_exit, rely on max_bars. Safety net: max_bars[S] = 80 for "fri" and 30 for "mon".

No other filters.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Stage A best design avg R on AUDJPY at entry_day = fri <= 0 or design t < 1. (2) Control: at the same entry_utc, exit_utc and sl_atr, avg R(fri) - avg R(mon) must be >= 0.03 R in design; if the weekday-overnight control earns as much as the weekend hold, the result is overnight carry drift (already known to give its swap back in crash months, prior_fx_carry) and the hypothesis dies regardless of sign. (3) Cross-market: at the chosen combination at least three of AUDJPY, NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD positive in design. (4) Regime: at least half of the design years positive and the check period positive with 2020 removed. (5) Interpretation rule, not a kill: if EURJPY is as good as the AUD/NZD crosses the premium is a JPY-risk premium, not carry. Honest expectations: a weekend premium of 4-8 pips including swap against a 120-240 pip stop is 0.02-0.06 R; with about 410 design trades and sd about 0.5 R, design t is 1.0-2.4, so this test is adequately powered for the first time in three cycles, but the effect may simply be absent.

hypotheses.why_different: Carry work in the index rebalanced monthly with trend and vol switches and holds positions through every day; the weekend premium is a two-day-per-week risk premium with the weekday-overnight control subtracted, so it is not carry drift. The atlas scanned single-weekday intraday windows of at most 8 hours and never held across a weekend; the Monday-gap tests (gap_cnyfix, edge_hunt) measured whether Monday gaps fill, not the Friday-to-Monday return. Equity overnight drift (eq_overnight_drift) was on US index CFDs at the European open. No prior test holds FX over the weekend by design.

director.direction_note: Cycle 5 scraps the two cycle-4 tests with lessons (tick volume is not a capitulation signal; shock days on majors continue, not reverse, at the one-day horizon; gold calendar seasonals reversed after 2010) and registers one hypothesis chosen for power: the weekend risk premium in carry crosses, about 410 design trades per market with a weekday-overnight control in the grid. This is the one horizon the programme has never held by design: every prior test is intraday, a single-day hold, or a monthly rebalance. If it dies, the price-only hypothesis space reachable with this data store is close to exhausted on the intraday, daily, calendar, cross-asset and volume dimensions, and the honest statement to the user is that further cycles are unlikely to find a new FX edge without external inputs (retail positioning, options risk reversals, FX swap basis, scheduled-event calendars) and that the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, which is a simulation task (gj-strat prop_sim, prop_risk_rules) rather than a hypothesis. Engine notes: the aux-market facility works; index feeds have coverage gaps (JP225 no Tokyo-morning bars 2015-2017, US100 no 21:00 UTC bars); D1 fills land at the 17:00 NY rollover, so daily-horizon specs should signal on the H1 bar closing at 20:00 UTC.

reasons: The idea is new and worth compute. No prior report holds FX across a weekend on purpose. The flow atlas used windows of at most 8 hours on single weekdays, and its series leave out Monday's weekend gap. gap_cnyfix measured Monday gap fills, not the Friday-to-Monday return. prior_fx_carry rebalanced monthly. So this is not a duplicate. The sample is about 410 trades per market in design, the first adequately powered test in three cycles, and the weekday-overnight control with matched hold lengths is good design (Fri 16:00->Mon 07:00 is about 15 trading hours, the same as Mon 16:00->Tue 07:00; Fri 20:00->Mon 00:00 is about 4, the same as Mon 20:00->Tue 00:00).

One claim in the rationale is false: 'paid twice: the weekend swap (three days of positive carry)'. Spot FX settles T+2, so the triple rollover falls on Wednesday, not Friday. The engine models it the same way (edge/engine/costs.py: 'one night of interest per 17:00 New York rollover held, three on Wednesday'), and the flow atlas NOTES show the Dukascopy price itself drops by about the interest differential at each 17:00 NY rollover, 3x on Wednesday ('the swap pays it back, so there is nothing to trade'). A Friday-to-Monday hold therefore crosses one 1x rollover, the same as the Monday control. Net carry is about zero minus the 1% markup in both arms. The weekend premium has to come from price alone, and the expectation '4-8 pips including swap' must be restated as price-only.

The cost estimate is too low. 'One spread plus slippage (0.9 + 0.4 pips) ... about 0.01 R' uses the all-hours median spread. Entry at Friday 20:00 UTC is the last 1-2 hours before the weekly close, when AUDJPY/NZDJPY spreads widen several-fold, and the 00:00 UTC Monday exit sits close to the thin Sunday-open book. The $7/lot commission adds about another pip on the JPY crosses. A realistic round trip is 3-4 pips, or about 0.025-0.03 R at sl_atr 1.5 and about 0.015 R at 3.0. That is the same size as the expected premium of 0.02-0.06 R, so the 1.5x gate is a real threat and the 2x soft gate probably fails at sl_atr 1.5. The control arm trades at normal mid-week spreads, so it carries lower costs than the Friday arm. That biases the comparison against the hypothesis, which is conservative and acceptable, but the cost gap should be reported.

The exit rule as written exits one hour early. 'Let X be the first H1 bar whose close time is at or after exit_utc ... exit_long[X - 1]' picks X = the 06:00 bar for a 07:00 exit (it closes at 07:00), so the position closes at that bar's open, 06:00. The entry rule (S = last bar closing at or before entry_utc, fill at the next open = entry_utc) is correct; the exit rule is inconsistent with it.

Kill rule (4), 'check period positive with 2020 removed', must not replace the hard gate. The weekend crash tail (2015-08-24, 2020-03-09/16, 2024-08-05 were all Monday-Asia events) is exactly the risk this premium is supposed to pay for. Dropping the crash year flatters the result. Both conditions must hold: check positive with all years (hard gate) and with 2020 removed.

Overfit risk is low. The hypothesis arms form a 2x2 family of session-anchored times (US afternoon de-risking vs last hour; Tokyo vs London re-risking) and come from theory. sl_atr barely binds: a 1.5-3 x ATR20 stop is rarely touched in about 4-15 trading hours, so it mostly rescales R and adds almost no selection freedom. The control is pre-registered with a numeric threshold. Remaining risk: the four primary markets (AUDJPY, NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD) are highly correlated, so '3 of 4 positive' is close to one observation, not three. The fri-minus-mon difference has a standard error of about 0.4 x sqrt(2/410) = 0.028 R, so the 0.03 R threshold is only about one standard error.
reviews.revisions: 1) Rationale and expectations: delete the 'three days of positive carry' / 'paid twice' claim. State that both arms cross exactly one 1x rollover (triple is Wednesday, in the engine and in Dukascopy prices), so net carry is about zero minus the 1% markup and the premium must come from price. Re-state the expected design avg R as a price-only premium after realistic weekend-edge costs: at least +0.02 R at sl_atr 1.5. 2) Cost statement: replace 'about 0.01 R' with an estimate from the actual Friday 20:00 UTC and Monday 00:00 UTC spreads, roughly 3-4 pips round trip including commission, 0.015-0.03 R. Report gross (before spread/commission) and net R for every arm, and report the mean entry and exit spread for each arm, so the fri/mon comparison can be read net of the spread difference. 3) Exit rule: X = the first H1 bar whose OPEN time (m.ts) is at or after exit_utc on D_exit, i.e. F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D_exit], hh, mm). Skip the trade if m.ts[X] is more than 60 minutes after the target (the max_bars net then does not apply). Set exit_long[X-1] = True when X-1 > S, so the close happens at the open of the bar starting at exit_utc. 4) Kill rule (4): the hard gate (check avg R > 0 over all check years) stays. 'Positive with 2020 removed' is an extra requirement, not a substitute. Also report 2015-08, 2020-03 and 2024-08 (holdout, at promotion only) weekend trades individually. 5) Control kill rule (2): keep the >= 0.03 R threshold and also report the t of the paired fri-minus-mon difference per market. Pre-register that the difference must be positive on at least 3 of the 4 AUD/NZD markets at the chosen combination, so one market cannot carry it. 6) Reduce max_bars to 24 for both arms. 80 H1 bars would let a missed Monday exit run to Wednesday and cross the triple rollover, mixing in exactly the carry the control is meant to exclude.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Follow the oracle pattern (strategies/oracle/m3_usd_bid.py) for clock times. Entry: for each UTC date D with weekday == entry_day (Fri = 4, Mon = 0 via F.weekday), ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D], eh, em). Require m.ts[ei] - (D + entry_utc) <= max_delay (60 min on H1) and ei >= 1. sig = ei - 1; entry_long[sig] = True, entry_type 0, valid_bars 1. sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * atr[ei], where atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, 20)); skip if not finite or <= 0. tp_dist NaN. Exit: D_exit = D + 3 days for 'fri', D + 1 day for 'mon'. xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D_exit], xh, xm). Require xi < m.n, xi - 1 > sig and m.ts[xi] - (D_exit + exit_utc) <= 60 min. Then exit_long[xi - 1] = True, max_bars[sig] = 24 as a safety net. Do NOT use 'first bar whose close >= exit_utc' (that exits one hour early). Note that a Monday 00:00 exit target can be preceded by Sunday-evening UTC bars (the market opens Sun 21:00/22:00 UTC); first_bar_at_or_after on the Monday date handles that correctly. Read every grid key from p (entry_day, entry_utc, exit_utc, sl_atr) and put all of them in PARAMS. Longs only on every market; no side logic needed. Do not filter on anything else (no vol filter, no rate filter): the hypothesis is unconditional. Loop over dates, not bars.
